text: Radar watched this volcano's lava spread for months. NASA's NISAR release combines seventeen observations of Krasheninnikov, in Russia's Kamchatka Peninsula, from December twenty twenty-five to August twenty twenty-six. The sequence follows material filling a crater and spreading outward. You are seeing processed radar measurements, not live video or a simulated eruption. Returning to the same place repeatedly helps scientists track changes at a remote volcano. It does not mean the satellite can predict the next eruption. Regular radar coverage adds another tool for monitoring natural hazards. Subscribe on YouTube at New Horizons underscore twenty-one, and like and follow on Instagram.
